classification.difficultyReason: Repeated product rule gives three derivatives. The student must then spot that each derivative adds 1 to the constant and generalise to the nth derivative. They must then reframe f^{(n)}(-10)=0 as the linear equation -10+2+n=0, and note that e^{-10} is never zero. The pattern generalisation and the linked setup of the final part make it harder than routine differentiation, but the pattern is signposted by the earlier parts.
